message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Validate Homebridge Docker Container
run-name: Validate Homebridge Docker Container - ${{ github.event.inputs.release_tag }} Release

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      release_tag:
        description: 'Release tag to validate (alpha, beta, or latest)'
        required: true
        type: string
        default: latest

  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_tag:
        description: 'Release tag to validate (alpha, beta, or latest)'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options:
          - alpha
          - beta
          - latest
        default: latest

concurrency:
  group: validate-docker-container
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  validate-container:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    
    steps:
    - name: Checkout
      uses: actions/checkout@v7

    - name: Set container image based on release tag
      id: set-image
      run: |
        echo "CONTAINER_IMAGE=ghcr.io/homebridge/homebridge:${{ inputs.release_tag }}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
        echo "EXPECTED_TAG=${{ inputs.release_tag }}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

    - name: Start Homebridge container
      working-directory: ./test
      run: |
        echo "Starting Homebridge container with image: ${{ steps.set-image.outputs.CONTAINER_IMAGE }}"
        export HOMEBRIDGE_IMAGE=${{ steps.set-image.outputs.CONTAINER_IMAGE }}
        docker compose up -d
        
        echo "Waiting for container to initialize..."
        sleep 15
        
        # Check if container is still running
        if ! docker compose ps | grep -q "Up"; then
          echo "❌ Container failed to start or exited unexpectedly"
          docker compose logs
          exit 1
        fi
        
        echo "✅ Container is running"

    - name: Validate Homebridge UI accessibility
      working-directory: ./test
      run: |
        echo "Testing Homebridge UI accessibility..."
        
        # Test UI accessibility with retries
        max_attempts=5
        attempt=1
        
        while [ $attempt -le $max_attempts ]; do
          echo "Attempt $attempt/$max_attempts: Checking UI accessibility..."
          
          if curl -f --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30 -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:8581 | grep -q "200"; then
            echo "✅ Homebridge UI is accessible (HTTP 200)"
            break
          elif [ $attempt -eq $max_attempts ]; then
            echo "❌ Homebridge UI is not accessible after $max_attempts attempts"
            
            # Show detailed debugging information
            echo "Container status:"
            docker compose ps
            echo "Container logs:"
            docker compose logs --tail 20
            echo "Port check:"
            netstat -tlnp | grep :8581 || echo "Port 8581 not listening"
            
            exit 1
          else
            echo "UI not ready yet, waiting 10 seconds..."
            sleep 10
            attempt=$((attempt + 1))
          fi
        done

    - name: Validate Homebridge service startup
      working-directory: ./test
      run: |
        echo "Validating Homebridge service startup..."
        
        # Check for Homebridge version in logs
        if docker compose logs | grep -q "Homebridge v"; then
          version=$(docker compose logs | grep "Homebridge v" | tail -1 | sed -n 's/.*Homebridge v\([0-9.]*\).*/\1/p')
          echo "✅ Homebridge service started successfully (version: $version)"
        else
          echo "❌ Homebridge version not found in logs"
          docker compose logs
          exit 1
        fi
        
        # Check for pairing code (indicates successful setup)
        if docker compose logs | grep -q "Enter this code"; then
          echo "✅ Homebridge setup completed with pairing code"
        else
          echo "⚠️  Pairing code not found - this may be normal for some configurations"
        fi
        
        # Check for any error messages
        if docker compose logs | grep -i error | grep -v "no such file or directory"; then
          echo "⚠️  Some errors found in logs (may be non-critical):"
          docker compose logs | grep -i error | grep -v "no such file or directory" | head -5
        fi

    - name: Test container health check
      working-directory: ./test
      run: |
        echo "Testing container health check..."
        
        # Wait a bit more for health check to stabilize
        sleep 5
        
        # Check container health status
        health_status=$(docker compose ps --format "table {{.Service}}\t{{.Status}}" | grep homebridge | awk '{print $2}')
        
        if echo "$health_status" | grep -q "Up"; then
          echo "✅ Container health check passed"
        else
          echo "❌ Container health check failed. Status: $health_status"
          docker compose ps
          exit 1
        fi

    - name: Validate hb-serivce status
      working-directory: ./test
      run: |
        echo "Validating hb-service status inside container..."
        docker compose exec homebridge sudo hb-service status || echo "⚠️ hb-service status failed"

        echo "Running hb-service view inside the container..."
        docker compose exec homebridge sudo hb-service view || echo "⚠️ hb-service view failed"

    - name: Validate version manifest
      run: |
        echo "Checking Docker manifest for ${{ inputs.release_tag }} release..."
        
        # Pull version manifest from container
        if docker run --rm ${{ steps.set-image.outputs.CONTAINER_IMAGE }} cat /opt/homebridge/Docker.manifest > manifest_output.txt 2>/dev/null; then
          echo "✅ Successfully retrieved Docker manifest"
          echo "Manifest preview:"
          head -10 manifest_output.txt
          
          # Check for expected components in manifest
          if grep -q "Ubuntu" manifest_output.txt && grep -q "Homebridge" manifest_output.txt; then
            echo "✅ Manifest contains expected components"
          else
            echo "⚠️  Manifest may be incomplete"
            cat manifest_output.txt
          fi
        else
          echo "⚠️  Could not retrieve Docker manifest (non-critical)"
        fi

    - name: Cleanup
      if: always()
      working-directory: ./test
      run: |
        echo "Cleaning up test environment..."
        docker compose down
        echo "✅ Cleanup completed"

    - name: Validation summary
      if: success()
      run: |
        echo "🎉 Container validation completed successfully!"
        echo "Release tag: ${{ inputs.release_tag }}"
        echo "Container image: ${{ steps.set-image.outputs.CONTAINER_IMAGE }}"
        echo "All validation checks passed:"
        echo "  ✅ Container started successfully"
        echo "  ✅ Homebridge UI accessible on port 8581"
        echo "  ✅ Homebridge service running"
        echo "  ✅ Container health check passed"
        echo "::notice::Validation completed successfully for tag ${{ inputs.release_tag }}"

    - name: Validation failure summary
      if: failure()
      run: |
        echo "❌ Container validation failed!"
        echo "Release tag: ${{ inputs.release_tag }}"
        echo "Container image: ${{ steps.set-image.outputs.CONTAINER_IMAGE }}"
        echo "Please review the logs above for details on the failure."
        echo "::error::Validation failed for tag ${{ inputs.release_tag }}"",
  "rationale": "The workflow uses a concurrency group with `cancel-in-progress: false`, meaning multiple triggered runs (e.g., repeated workflow_dispatch or rapid push events) will queue and all execute sequentially. The P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE pattern (from literature S01) shows that canceling superseded runs reduces duplicate work with estimated VM time reductions of 1.9% (free) and 4.1% (paid). This workflow validates Docker container images where a newer validation run supersedes an older one—there is no need to complete an older validation once a newer one starts. The change is minimal, preserves all validation steps and coverage, and only affects behavior when multiple runs are triggered for the same concurrency group. No contraindications apply: this is not a release/deployment workflow, and the concurrency group is specific to this validation workflow.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE"]
}
message.reasoning:
Let me analyze the workflow and the evidence to determine if there's a suitable CI optimization.

The workflow is for validating a Homebridge Docker container. It:
1. Checks out code
2. Sets container image based on release tag
3. Starts Homebridge container with docker compose
4. Validates UI accessibility with retries
5. Validates service startup
6. Tests container health check
7. Validates hb-service status
8. Validates version manifest
9. Cleans up

Key characteristics:
- Single job (no matrix)
- Runs on ubuntu-latest
- Has timeout-minutes: 15
- Uses docker compose to start container
- Has multiple validation steps with retries and sleeps
- No caching currently
- No fail-fast (single job)
- Concurrency group with cancel-in-progress: false

Looking at the evidence:
1. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT experiment shows 26.8% elapsed savings by adding timeout-minutes: 5 to a job that had no timeout
2. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST experiments show setting fail-fast: true on matrix jobs
3. P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE pattern for canceling superseded runs
4. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE for caching dependencies

For this workflow:
- It already has timeout-minutes: 15 (so P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT not applicable as it already has a timeout)
- It's a single job, not a matrix (so P-LIT-FAIL-FAST not applicable)
- It has concurrency with cancel-in-progress: false (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE could be relevant - changing to true would cancel superseded runs)
- No dependency caching (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE could be relevant but this workflow doesn't install npm dependencies - it uses docker)

Let me check the workflow more carefully:
- It uses `actions/checkout@v7` 
- It runs docker compose commands
- No npm ci or similar dependency installation
- The validation is all about the docker container

The P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE pattern seems most relevant here. The workflow has:
```yaml
concurrency:
  group: validate-docker-container
  cancel-in-progress: false
```

Changing `cancel-in-progress: false` to `cancel-in-progress: true` would cancel superseded runs when a new workflow is triggered for the same concurrency group. This is supported by the P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE pattern which shows estimated VM time reduction of 1.9% (free) and 4.1% (paid).

The evidence for P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE includes:
- Pattern from literature (S01 paper)
- Experiment examples showing the change from `cancel-in-progress: false` to `cancel-in-progress: true`

This is a minimal, safe change that preserves all build and test coverage. It only affects behavior when multiple runs are triggered for the same workflow (e.g., multiple workflow_dispatch or push events).

Let me verify the preconditions for P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE:
- "Runs represent the same workflow and branch or PR" - yes, same workflow
- "A newer revision supersedes older checks" - yes, for validation of docker container, newer run supersedes older

Contraindications:
- "Release or deployment work" - this is validation, not release/deployment
- "Distinct branches share a cancellation group" - the group is "validate-docker-container" which seems specific to this workflow

This seems like a valid optimization. Let me also check if there's evidence from the experiment records. Looking at the evidence, I see experiment examples for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT and P-LIT-FAIL-FAST, but not directly for P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE. However, the pattern catalogue includes P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE with reported results.

The instruction says "Use only supported evidence IDs; APPLY requires at least one." The pattern catalogue entries are evidence with document_ids like "pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE". I should use those.

Let me propose the change: set `cancel-in-progress: true` in the concurrency section.

This is a minimal change that:
1. Preserves all validation steps
2. Only cancels superseded runs (when a new validation is triggered before the previous one completes)
3. Is supported by the P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE pattern
4. Doesn't weaken permissions or add privileged actions

I'll use evidence_id "pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE" from the pattern catalogue.
